findings.label: Skilled's connector surface is one repo-wide UTCP config with 14 MCP servers, each declared as a manual_call_templates entry with call_template_type mcp and a config.mcpServers block.
Server environment comes from one dotenv file via load_variables_from with variable_loader_type dotenv and an env_file_path, so every server and every bot shares one secret path today.
The MCP surface is reached through one launcher: .mcp.json declares a single code_mode server that runs .skilled/bin/mcp-code-mode-launcher.cjs with UTCP_CONFIG_FILE.
The launcher resolves a Node interpreter and hands off to the MCP server under it; it is 181 lines and does no per-bot filtering.
The runner already has an environment allowlist: commonlyAdmittedKeys derives the keys every executor kind admits and commonEnv gives a precheck only that part.

The smallest registry is a per-run filtered UTCP config: the runner writes a temporary config containing only the servers the bot's apps list names and points UTCP_CONFIG_FILE at it, which is one file write and one environment variable on machinery that already exists.
The grant belongs in BOT.md frontmatter beside posture, because FRONTMATTER_KEYS is already the closed set of bot fields and apps is one more.
The record belongs on HonoredPosture beside secretsUsed, so one block answers what a run could reach and what it used.
OpenBot's per-action grant is the model to copy at the smallest scale: each app comes with the actions it offers and the bots that may use each one.
No OAuth server is needed for a small team: OpenBot's own OAuth client is the exception for vendors that refuse dynamic registration, and turnstone's per-user OAuth is opt-in and dark by default.

ruledOut.reason: it is the largest single piece of OpenBot's app layer and the one a small team can skip, because a shared account or a key covers the common case
they need a sign-in surface and a session store, while a small team on one host can share one account per app, which is OpenBot's own shared account mode
none of the eight repos ships one a small team would use, and the UTCP config already names the servers this team actually has
